text: A function that reads only its arguments and does nothing but return a value — movable, cacheable, testable in isolation, and safe on several threads — is called a ___ function.
explanation: The related property is referential transparency: a call can be replaced by its result without changing the program's meaning. It is what the parallel counter lacked and what the stream assumed. None of this requires a lambda — pure methods were available since Chapter 11 — but lambdas make the pure parts small enough to pass around, which turns a discipline into a convenience.
